input.task: Sort the catalogue by price, low to high, and name the cheapest product.

provenance: written before the M4 progress stream existed. Watched red twice: on the missing on_step hook (TypeError, the pre-M4 state), and on the honesty mutation that matters — emitting only steps whose execution raised nothing. Under that mutation the run still returns success, the terminal status still matches, and the emitted ids are still in order (1,3,4); only emits_failed_attempt goes red, on the superseded text-tier click at #2. The M4 claim under test is 'a stranger can watch the run and inspect a failure' — a stream that quietly drops the attempts a ladder superseded would let a reviewer watch this exact run, see two tidy steps, and never learn that the text tier died and the agent relocated. The scenario is deliberately the recovery case (button-text-renamed), because it is the only fixture run whose trace contains an attempt that FAILED and was superseded — a stream tested on a clean run cannot fail this way.

triage.note: the failure mode is presentational, not executional: the run is correct either way, so nothing else in the suite goes red if the viewer lies by omission. That is exactly why it needs its own case — the trace is the deliverable evidence, and a viewer that shows a prettier run than the one that happened is honesty debt, not a UI bug.
